rules.rule: Never use `any`. Use `unknown` for unknown shapes (narrow with type guards) or `Record<string, unknown>` for objects with unknown structure. `Record<string, any>` only with a justifying comment.
Avoid the `!` non-null assertion operator. Use optional chaining or a type guard. Only acceptable with a justifying biome-ignore comment.
Mark inputs and interface fields as `readonly` when the value won't change. Use `readonly T[]` over `T[]` for array inputs.
Utility functions that operate on objects should use generics like `<T, K extends keyof T>` to preserve return types. Don't accept `object` or cast.
Use tagged unions like `{ status: 'loading' } | { status: 'success'; data: T }` for state instead of multiple boolean flags.

Components render UI and call event handlers. Business logic (validation, transformation, contract calls) belongs in pure helpers like `*.handlers.ts`, `*.transactions.ts`, or `helpers/`. Flag components mixing fetch logic, encoding, validation, and rendering.
Never fetch data in `useEffect`. Use TanStack Query (`useQuery`, `useQueries`, `useSuspenseQuery`). Manual `useState` + `useEffect` + `setLoading/setError` patterns are forbidden.
Multi-step transaction flows must use an XState machine. Flag `useEffect` that calls `transactionManager.startTransaction()` based on another transaction's state, or `hasTriggered`-style guard flags.

Use `const Component = (props) => {}` for React components. Reserve `function` declarations for utilities. Exception: TanStack Router `RouteComponent` declared via `createFileRoute(...)({ component })` may use `function`.
Effects in components must be extracted to a named custom hook unless: ≤5 lines, no async logic, no domain logic, no external dependencies. Does not apply inside custom hooks themselves.

Custom hooks wrap framework/browser APIs (DOM, localStorage, wagmi, TanStack hooks, XState). Business logic belongs in pure functions called from event handlers. Flag hooks with 30+ lines of validation/encoding logic.
Use `ts-pattern`'s `match()` for 3+ branches or state discrimination. Avoid nested ternaries and chained `&&` with falsy-prone values (`0`, `''`, `null`).
Don't mutate data structures. Use spreads, `map`, `filter` over `push`/`splice`/direct field assignment on shared state.
When using `useMutation`, read `mutation.isPending`, `mutation.isSuccess`, `mutation.data` directly. Don't create derived `useState` like `const isSubmitting = mutation.isPending`.
Query helpers should export `getXxxQueryOptions(params)` that wraps `ResultFn` data fetchers via `resultQueryOptions`. Call sites use `useQuery(getXxxQueryOptions(...))` — no custom hook wrapper.

TanStack Query `data` returned via `resultQueryOptions` is already unwrapped; `error` is the `TaggedError` instance. Always check `isLoading`, `error`, `!data` separately. Don't call `.match()` or read `.value` on `data`.
Use `createQueryKey<'name', Params>()` helper with params as a single object: `recordsQueryKey({ name, texts })`, not `['records', name, texts]`. Object form enables partial invalidation.
When query B depends on query A's data, split into separate components rather than gating B with `enabled: !!a.data` in the same component.
Don't combine query states with `||` (`isLoading: a.isLoading || b.isLoading`). Render each section's loading/error states independently so users see partial data.
When iterating over N items, use `useQueries({ queries: items.map(...) })` rather than N parallel `useQuery` calls.

Never mix `Result` with `try/catch` inside a function that returns `Result`. Pick one approach per function. `try/catch` is acceptable at the outermost event-handler boundary calling helpers that throw.
Never write `.then(r => { if (r.isErr()) throw r.error; return r.value })`. Chain Results with `.andThen()` or yield in a `ResultFn` generator.
Define error classes extending `TaggedError('NAME')<{ cause: unknown }>` per operation. Enables discriminated-union matching on errors.
Multi-step async pipelines that return `Result` should use `ResultFn(async function* () { ... })` with `yield*` to chain Results without manual error propagation.
Wrap throwing sync code with `fromSync` (from `@ens-apps/utils`) or `fromThrowable` (from `neverthrow`). Don't `try/catch` around sync code that should return `Result`.
Inside `ResultFn` generators, `yield*` already handles async Results. Writing `yield* await ResultAsync.fromPromise(...)` is redundant — drop the `await`.
In event handlers, prefer `if (result.isErr()) return` over `.match()`. `.match()` belongs in functional composition, not imperative UI code.
All blockchain numeric values (wei, durations in seconds, prices, expiries, gas) must be `bigint`. Use literal `n` suffix or `BigInt()`. No `number` for on-chain numerics.
Never call `createPublicClient` or `createWalletClient` inside components or render functions. Use shared clients via `usePublicClient`, `useWalletClient`, or `safeGetClient`.
Inside `ResultFn` data helpers, get the public client via `yield* safeGetClient()` rather than constructing or fetching it directly.
User-supplied ENS names must pass through `normalize` from `viem/ens` before being used in contract calls or queries.
When wrapping an ENSjs function with a local helper of the same name, import as `getXxx as ensjs_getXxx` (or `ensjsGetXxx`). Also import the matching `GetXxxErrorType` for `TaggedError.cause` typing.
Inside `@ensdomains/ensjs`, writes split into `xxxWriteParameters` (returns params) and `xxx` (executes). App-level helpers may use the single request-builder pattern instead.
Multi-step transaction flows must use the transaction-manager, not wagmi's `useWriteContract`. Flag direct wagmi writes for flows that chain multiple transactions.
Components `PascalCase.tsx`, utilities `camelCase.ts`, hooks `use*.ts`, types `*.types.ts`, handlers `*.handlers.ts`, machines `*.machine.ts`, mocks `*.mock.ts` or `MOCK.ts`, tests `*.test.ts(x)`.
Boolean variables and props use `is*`, `has*`, `should*`, or `can*` prefixes. Flag bare nouns/verbs (e.g. `loading` → `isLoading`, `editRecords` → `canEditRecords`).
True constants use `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` (addresses, durations, magic numbers). Config objects stay `camelCase`.
Mock data lives in `*.mock.ts` files and is gated by `import.meta.env.DEV` or a feature flag. Never mix mock data into production code paths.
Use `cn` from `@/lib/utils` for conflict-resolving Tailwind class merges. Don't introduce `tw`/`twm` unless the surrounding area already uses them.
Avoid arbitrary Tailwind values like `w-[37px]`, `text-[#3B82F6]`. Use design tokens (`size-9`, `text-primary`). Allowed only with a justifying inline comment.
Size Lucide icons with `className="size-4"`, not `size={16}` or `width={16} height={16}` props.
No emojis in source code unless the user explicitly requested them.
Use `focus-visible:ring-*` classes for keyboard focus. Don't strip `outline` without a replacement, and don't use `:focus` for the ring (it triggers on mouse clicks too).
Buttons need `type="button"` unless inside a form needing submit semantics.
Non-button elements with `onClick` need `onKeyDown` (Enter/Space), `role`, and `tabIndex` — or should be a `<button>` instead.
`<label htmlFor="x">` must match an `<input id="x">`. Use `useId()` to generate ids.
Don't `useMemo`/`useCallback` for cheap operations or values not used as a dependency. Flag clearly wasteful cases (e.g. memoizing a string concat).
When a value is passed as a dependency to `useEffect`, `useQuery`, or a memoized child, memoize the parent to prevent infinite loops or refetches.

Many props (~10+) can signal a component doing too much. If it reads that way, suggest a fitting remedy — grouping related props into an object, composition, or splitting — and use judgement; other approaches are fine. See STYLEGUIDE.md 'Number of Props'.
Files over ~500 lines are a soft signal the file may do too much; suggest splitting by responsibility, but leave cohesive files alone. See STYLEGUIDE.md 'Component Size and Complexity'.

Prefer one primary component per file. Small co-located helpers are fine, even with a little local state; flag only when several substantial components in one file would clearly be better split out. See STYLEGUIDE.md.
